prompt: Sound travels much faster through a steel rail than through air — roughly 5,000 metres per second instead of about 343. Why is it so much faster in steel?

options.text: Particles in steel are much closer together and tightly linked, so vibrations pass from one to the next far faster than in air
Steel is heavier than air, and heavier materials always carry sound faster
Sound in steel is carried by electric currents, which travel near light speed
Air slows sound down only because wind pushes against it

explanation: Sound is a vibration passed from particle to particle. In steel the particles are packed tightly and held in a stiff, elastic solid, so each vibration is handed on much faster than in air, where molecules are far apart — about 5,000 metres per second versus about 343.
